messages:
anya: Heads-up — we're seeing a regression in prefix cache hit-rate for SDK clients using the new cache negotiation header. Hit-rate dropped ~20% after the runtime deploy :eyes:

matt: Oh no. Do we have a perf dump or profiler trace?

sophie: Can you paste a failing request/headers example so we can reproduce quickly?

anya: Sure — minimal failing headers we saw in logs:
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.internal
X-Redwood-Cache: negotiate
X-Redwood-Client-Version: 2.14.0
Cache-Opt: client-prefetch=1
Content-Type: application/json
```
We warm up prefixes (~10k warmup calls) with the header, then mixed traffic shows miss ratio rises after ~30 minutes.

jordan: Noted — during the kernel-selection refactor (commit abc123) we canonicalized prompt keys slightly differently. I suspect the hashing change + batching reorder is causing different key bytes for some multiline prompts.

matt: Profiler shows misses correlate with high sequence-length variance. Our batching heuristics started grouping by arrival order which causes more frequent KV evictions for long-tail prefixes. Also noticed retries create new cache-IDs.

sophie: Is the incident limited to streaming endpoints? We've seen clients reconnect streams mid-response and that triggers a retry flow that seems to bypass cache re-use.

anya: Repro steps we used: 1) send N warmup requests with identical prefix header negotiate; 2) send mixed prompts with varied continuation lengths; 3) simulate flaky network to force streaming reconnects. Miss rate spikes only when retries/reconnects happen.

infra-bot: deploy_bot: rolled back runtime v1.18.3 -> v1.18.2 at 2026-03-17T14:55Z (automatic rollback due to perf regression alert)

jordan: OK. Two likely causes: (1) key canonicalization delta in kernel refactor, (2) cache-negotiation handshake semantics — currently the server treats negotiate as stateless and may issue a new nonce/cache-id per connection, so retry creates a distinct cache entry.

matt: Proposal — server should return an explicit Cache-Id header when accepting negotiation and only change it on real invalidation. Clients must reuse Cache-Id across retries. Also revert the small key-canonicalization change for now and add a deterministic normalizer for newlines and whitespace in prompt keys.

sophie: SDK changes needed: honor Cache-Id from server, include header in retry attempts, and avoid re-sending warmup sequences if Cache-Id unchanged. For streaming: checkpoint stream position and resume using the same cache-id, not rewarm.

anya: Action items: matt -> server patch to emit Cache-Id and stable handshake; jordan -> roll back canonicalization and add key-normalizer; sophie -> SDK update to reuse cache-id and handle partial-stream reconnects without full rewarm. I'll add dark-launch telemetry to measure impact before a full rollout.

jordan: I'll open a PR with a regression test that simulates a client reconnect during a mid-stream event and asserts no rewarm or duplicate warmup writes to KV. Test will fuzz sequence lengths and batching sizes.

matt: Quick server patch drafted. Adds response headers: `X-Redwood-Cache-Accept: yes` and `X-Redwood-Cache-Id: <hex>`; semantics: if client sends same Cache-Id on retries we treat it as the same warmup. Also rework batching eviction window to favor long-lived prefixes.

sophie: I'll update the JS/py SDKs to read X-Redwood-Cache-Id and stash it on the client instance. Retries will attach the same id and backoff will be idempotent. Also adding test to simulate network jitter during streaming.

anya: Nice. Can we add a temporary telemetry dimension `cache_negotiation.cache_id_reuse` and `cache_negotiation.miss_delta` so we can compare v1.18.2 vs dark-launch on v1.18.3?

jordan: Yep. I'll add those to the perf dashboard (prefix-cache hit-rate, miss-by-retry-reason).

anya: Assigning: matt (server patch), jordan (tests & dashboard), sophie (SDK). We'll watch the hit-rate dashboard and roll forward when miss delta is <2%. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
